{"id": "b3348279-10b9-42c3-93b2-00f91f3ad4a1", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Moving the Bedrock calls to eu-west-1 should fix this. These are the options, starting with the one I'd try first.

**1. Call Bedrock in eu-west-1 (recommended)**
- Point your Bedrock Runtime client at `eu-west-1`. This removes the cross-Atlantic hop.
- If the model is available in-Region there, use its regular model ID.
- If it's only offered through an inference profile, use the **EU geographic inference profile ID**. That's the model ID with an `eu.` prefix. Bedrock then routes requests across EU Regions only, so your data stays in the EU.
- Not every model is available in-Region in eu-west-1. Check the Regional availability page for your model. To see what your account can use, run `aws bedrock list-inference-profiles --region eu-west-1`.

**2. Use a global inference profile, if data residency allows**
- Global profiles let Bedrock pick the best Region. They can help with throughput and capacity.
- They don't guarantee the processing Region is close to you, so they may not fix latency. If you have EU residency requirements, don't use them.

**3. Check what else moved or stayed behind**
- **Prompt and context sources:** if your app fetches data from us-east-1 before calling Bedrock (S3, DynamoDB, a vector store or knowledge base), those calls have the same latency problem.
- **Knowledge Bases, Guardrails, Agents:** these are Regional resources. You'll need to recreate them in eu-west-1 and update the IDs in your config.
- **IAM and quotas:** quotas are per Region and per model, so request increases for eu-west-1 before you cut over. Model access also needs to be enabled there.
- **VPC endpoints:** if you use PrivateLink, create a `bedrock-runtime` interface endpoint in your eu-west-1 VPC. Otherwise traffic goes out over NAT and the public internet.
- **Client settings:** keep connections alive and reuse the client. Streaming (`ConverseStream`/`InvokeModelWithResponseStream`) improves time-to-first-token. Set sensible timeouts so retries to a distant Region don't pile up.

If the app is still slow after you switch to eu-west-1, the cause is probably model-side latency or prompt size. I can look at your Bedrock invocation latency metrics in CloudWatch (`InvocationLatency`, and time-to-first-token if you stream) to compare Regions. I can also check which Bedrock models and inference profiles your account can use in eu-west-1. Tell me the model you use and which account to check.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
